parts.note: original means new, never seen before
broom is a yellow-flowered shrub

explanation.surface: A pioneering gardener with a passion for greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'new broom' is a newcomer full of zeal for sweeping changes, from the saying that a new broom sweeps clean.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an eager newcomer keen to reform things, an enthusiast for change.

clue.text: Entrance has unusual name associated with us

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of name are set out in a strange new order

parts.note: our is the possessive form belonging to us

explanation.surface: A doorway bears an odd name linked to the speakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' is the verb (en-TRANCE, to delight), not a doorway. 'unusual' rearranges NAME to ENAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to charm and captivate them, synonymous with making them fall in love.

parts.note: a bluff is a steep headland, a head of land
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness place names

explanation.surface: Blunt temperament shown in a face-off between two rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'head-to-head confrontation' is two headlands placed face to face; 'confrontation' merely dresses the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluffness is a blunt, frank, hearty manner of speaking, the trait of being plain-spoken.

parts.note: Madge is an old dialect name for the barn owl, so its young are baby birds of that kind, not a woman's children

explanation.walkthrough: Madge looks like a woman's name; it is an old country name for the barn owl.
explanation.definitionFit: Young birds of the barn owl are its chicks, the offspring of a Madge.

clue.text: Greater! resolution needed when this is taken in hand

definitions.text: Greater! resolution needed when this is taken in hand

parts.words: Greater! resolution needed when this is taken in hand
parts.note: a hand-held lens makes things look bigger and shows fine detail, so it gives enlargement and resolving power when held

explanation.walkthrough: 'resolution' suggests determination; here it is optical resolution, the sharpness of detail a lens gives.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand lens enlarges an object's image and reveals fine detail, the optical sense of resolution.

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national railway
aces are unreturnable serves in tennis

explanation.surface: Essential backing given by the providers of public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: BR was British Rail, Britain's state railway; an ace is a tennis serve the opponent cannot touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Braces are the straps holding up trousers, a crucial means of keeping them in place.

clue.text: The Lancers may be on parade here?

definitions.text: The Lancers may be on parade here?

parts.words: The Lancers may be on parade here?
parts.note: the Lancers is a quadrille, a set dance, not a cavalry regiment, so it is performed in a dance hall

explanation.walkthrough: The Lancers reads as a cavalry regiment on the parade ground; it is a nineteenth-century square dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A large hall for formal dancing is where a quadrille such as the Lancers would be danced.

indicators.note: without tells us the hesitation sound is dropped from the holder

parts.note: a container is a vessel that holds things
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Fit someone in at a stand without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holder' looks like the definition beside 'Accommodate'; 'without' takes away the hesitation sound, leaving a verb meaning to hold.
explanation.definitionFit: To contain is to hold or have room for, as a hall may accommodate a crowd.

explanation.surface: Rules governing how a garden border is planted.
explanation.definitionFit: Standards are rules or benchmarks; in gardening, standards are roses or shrubs trained on a single tall stem for beds.

explanation.surface: A typewriter or piano needing to be worked by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Manual means operated by hand; an organ's manual is one of its keyboards played with the hands.

clue.text: Source of wealth could be mine?

definitions.text: Source of wealth could be mine?

parts.words: Source of wealth could be mine?
parts.note: reads as a boast of possession, but mine is a pit: an Indian city famed for its diamond mines became a byword for riches

explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' reads as a possessive; the name belonged to an old Indian fortress city whose diamond mines made it a byword for riches.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian city's legendary diamond workings made its name a byword for any rich source of treasure.

parts.note: not a newspaper round but scraps of coloured paper showered over a bride and groom

explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper delivery' suggests a newspaper round; it is the shower of paper scraps thrown at a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Small coloured paper pieces are thrown over a bride and groom as they leave the ceremony.

indicators.note: returns means the word for the artist is read backwards

parts.note: a drawer is one who draws, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter comes back to collect extra payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses DRAWER (one who draws).
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is a payment or prize given in recognition, much like a bonus.

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A Native American perished for his faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a system of religious faith or a set of principles held.

explanation.surface: A woman waiting at table on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name; also a fruit pudding in a mould, a dessert served at the table (board).

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
an opener is a batsman who starts the innings in cricket

explanation.surface: An unexpected glance at the man at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opener is one of the two batsmen who begin the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: Something startling or revealing that shocks by its unexpectedness.

clue.text: One likely to put a good face on things

definitions.text: One likely to put a good face on things

parts.words: One likely to put a good face on things
parts.note: sounds like an optimist but is a craftsman who coats objects with a glossy vitreous surface

explanation.walkthrough: 'put a good face on things' suggests looking on the bright side; literally it is giving objects a fine glazed surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who coats metal or pottery with a glassy glaze gives objects an attractive surface.

clue.text: Panorama ran the show containing the flower of the poets

indicators.note: the words Panorama ran the show what they contain, the run of letters across them

explanation.surface: A television documentary series presented the poets' favourite bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Panorama is a long-running BBC current-affairs programme; the answer runs across 'PanorAMA RAN THe'.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetry this is an imaginary unfading bloom, a symbol of immortality.

parts.note: to tickle someone is to amuse them

indicators.note: say signals that the following piece is a sound-alike of the word spoken

parts.note: intended means meant

explanation.surface: A joke meant to entertain, by way of a distraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' makes MEANT sound like MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment or a pastime that diverts attention and gives pleasure.

clue.text: Is in audition, you listen carelessly to the instrument

indicators.note: in audition means as heard, so the word you is given by its spoken letter

parts.note: the letter U sounds like you

indicators.note: carelessly says the letters of listen are jumbled without care

explanation.surface: At a tryout, a musician hears the instrument sloppily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In audition' means as heard, so the word 'you' gives just the letter that sounds like it; 'carelessly' jumbles the next word, and 'Is' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or implement, an instrument for practical use.

explanation.surface: Someone hurries off to play a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to dash quickly; darts is also the pub sport of throwing small arrows at a board.

clue.text: Fool the French and quietly run away

parts.note: to fool is to trick
le is the French for the

explanation.surface: Deceive the French and sneak off.
explanation.definitionFit: To trickle is to flow away slowly in a thin stream, a gentle, unobtrusive running off.

clue.text: Shock of art reform by University Master

indicators.note: reform means the letters of art are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: MA is Master of Arts

explanation.surface: Upheaval as an academic overhauls art teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges ART to TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A trauma is a severe emotional or physical jolt or injury.

definitions.note: the answer is the plural of a German word for a song; the clue's singular stands for the genre

indicators.note: sounds signals that the answer is spoken like the phrase that follows

parts.note: the one in front, the leader, is the likely winner

explanation.surface: The tune sounds like the favourite to win.
explanation.walkthrough: Lieder (plural of Lied) are German art songs, as by Schubert; the clue uses 'Song' for the form.
explanation.definitionFit: German Romantic art songs for voice and piano form a recognised genre.

indicators.note: variegated means of mixed colours, so the letters of Dig near a are mixed up

explanation.surface: Excavate beside a shrub with mottled leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variegated' rearranges DIGNEARA.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardenia is an evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers.

clue.text: Traveller with first class return to island

parts.note: Abel Tasman was a Dutch explorer and seafarer

indicators.note: return means the letters for first class are turned back to front

parts.note: A1 means first class, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A voyager comes back in luxury to an isle.
explanation.walkthrough: The island is named after Abel Tasman, the Dutch explorer; A1, meaning first-rate, is read as letters, and 'return' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian state is an island south of the mainland.

parts.note: UN is the United Nations organisation
to like is to admire

explanation.surface: A body that one admires stands apart from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlike means dissimilar, not resembling something else.

clue.text: Artefact revealed by the oil rig

indicators.note: rig as a verb means to manipulate or fix, so the letters of the oil are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient object turned up by an offshore drilling platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rig' looks like an oil platform; as a verb it rearranges THEOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: An eolith is a crudely chipped flint thought to be a primitive human-made tool.

parts.note: main is the poetic word for the ocean, so a colour of the ocean, not a primary colour

explanation.walkthrough: 'main' suggests principal colours; it is the old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluish-green shade like that of ocean water.
